_about: answer = index of the right option (shuffled on screen); evidence = supporting sentence, review only; hint = gentle "look again" line.

demonstration.q: What did the Time Traveller say every real body has besides length, breadth and thickness?
demonstration.evidence: it must have Length, Breadth, Thickness, and—Duration.

demonstration.q: Why did the model machine vanish?
options: The lever sent it gliding off through time
demonstration.evidence: Now I want you clearly to understand that this lever, being pressed over, sends the machine gliding into the future, and this other reverses the motion.

demonstration.q: The Time Traveller came in dusty, limping and hungry. What did that suggest to his guests?
options: He had been on a real and difficult journey
demonstration.evidence: His coat was dusty and dirty, and smeared with green down the sleeves; his hair disordered, and as it seemed to me greyer—either with dust and dirt or because its colour had actually faded.
demonstration.hint: Look again at how he arrives.

through-time.q: How did night and day look as he went faster?
options: Night followed day like the flapping of a black wing
It stayed night all the time
through-time.evidence: As I put on pace, night followed day like the flapping of a black wing.

through-time.q: Why did the travelling feel like a switchback?
options: It was a helpless headlong motion
The machine went up and down hills
through-time.evidence: There is a feeling exactly like that one has upon a switchback—of a helpless headlong motion!
through-time.hint: Look again at how it felt.

through-time.q: Snow flashed across the world, then the green of spring. What was he seeing?
through-time.evidence: minute by minute the white snow flashed across the world, and vanished, and was followed by the bright, brief green of spring.
through-time.hint: Think about how fast he is going.

eloi.q: What did one of the little people put round his neck?
eloi.evidence: Then came one laughing towards me, carrying a chain of beautiful flowers altogether new to me, and put it about my neck.

eloi.q: Why did he take the little levers off the machine?
options: So nobody could set it in motion
To give them as a present
eloi.evidence: Happily then, when it was not too late, I thought of a danger I had hitherto forgotten, and reaching over the bars of the machine I unscrewed the little levers that would set it in motion, and put these in my pocket.
eloi.hint: Look again at the little pink hands.

eloi.q: He expected the people of the future to be far ahead of us. Why was he surprised?
options: They seemed gentle and childlike, not wise
eloi.evidence: You see I had always anticipated that the people of the year Eight Hundred and Two Thousand odd would be incredibly in front of us in knowledge, art, everything.
eloi.hint: Look again at what he thought.

missing-machine.q: What did he find when he got back to the little lawn?
missing-machine.hint: Look again at the moonlit lawn.

options: He rescued her when she was drifting downstream
missing-machine.evidence: When I realized this, I hurriedly slipped off my clothes, and, wading in at a point lower down, I caught the poor mite and drew her safe to land.
missing-machine.hint: Look again at the bathers in the river.

missing-machine.q: The pedestal of the sphinx was hollow. Why was that important?
options: The machine could have been hidden inside it
It was a good place to sleep
missing-machine.hint: Think about the groove in the turf.

wells.q: What did he use to climb down the well?
options: Climbing hooks on the side of the shaft
wells.evidence: I said, kissing her; and then putting her down, I began to feel over the parapet for the climbing hooks.
wells.hint: Look again at the top of the well.

wells.q: Why were the little Upper-world people afraid of the dark?
options: The Morlocks came out in the dark nights
They could not see the flowers
wells.evidence: And I now understood to some slight degree at least the reason of the fear of the little Upper-world people for the dark.
wells.hint: Look again at the Dark Nights.

wells.q: The creatures below retreated from his match. What does that show about them?
options: They live in darkness and dislike light
wells.evidence: Starting up in the darkness I snatched at my matches and, hastily striking one, I saw three stooping white creatures similar to the one I had seen above ground in the ruin, hastily retreating before the light.

palace.q: What did he find in an airtight case?
palace.evidence: And at last, in one of the really airtight cases, I found a box of matches.

palace.q: What had happened to the books in the library?
options: They had rotted into brown and charred rags
They were all in perfect condition
palace.evidence: The brown and charred rags that hung from the sides of it, I presently recognized as the decaying vestiges of books.

palace.q: The rotting library made him think of the “enormous waste of labour”. Why?
options: All that knowledge had been lost forever
palace.evidence: But as it was, the thing that struck me with keenest force was the enormous waste of labour to which this sombre wilderness of rotting paper testified.
palace.hint: Think about what books are for.

forest.q: What did he gather to make a fire?
forest.evidence: Accordingly, as we went along I gathered any sticks or dried grass I saw, and presently had my arms full of such litter.
forest.hint: Look again at the walk to the forest.

forest.q: Why was fire so strange to Weena?
options: The art of fire-making had been forgotten
forest.evidence: In this decadence, too, the art of fire-making had been forgotten on the earth.

forest.q: When he reached the sphinx, the bronze valves were open. Why does he call it a “meek surrender”?
options: It looked too easy — it was a trap
forest.evidence: So here, after all my elaborate preparations for the siege of the White Sphinx, was a meek surrender.
forest.hint: Look again at what happens next.

vault.q: What colour was the sun in the far future?
vault.evidence: At last, some time before I stopped, the sun, red and very large, halted motionless upon the horizon, a vast dome glowing with a dull heat, and now and then suffering a momentary extinction.

vault.q: What creatures did he see on the red beach?
vault.evidence: Then I saw the thing was really a monstrous crablike creature.

vault.q: What could the Medical Man not identify?
vault.evidence: “It’s a curious thing,” said the Medical Man; “but I certainly don’t know the natural order of these flowers.
vault.hint: Think about the evidence on the table.

vault.q: What did the Time Traveller take with him when he left again?
options: A small camera and a knapsack
vault.evidence: He had a small camera under one arm and a knapsack under the other.

vault.q: What did the two white flowers prove to the narrator?
options: That gratitude and tenderness still lived on
That the Time Traveller was lying
vault.evidence: And I have by me, for my comfort, two strange white flowers—shrivelled now, and brown and flat and brittle—to witness that even when mind and strength had gone, gratitude and a mutual tenderness still lived on in the heart of man.

vault.q: Where had the Morlocks hidden the machine?
options: Inside the pedestal of the White Sphinx
In the Palace of Green Porcelain
vault.evidence: That gives you the exact distance from my little lawn to the pedestal of the White Sphinx, into which the Morlocks had carried my machine.
